title: Normalized cross-project fractal-renderer benchmark record
description: One record = one (project, impl, workload) timing measurement, normalized from whatever native benchmark tool produced it (Criterion, Google Benchmark, or a hand-rolled bench_runner). Every measurement any project produces gets a record here, including ones with no peer in any other project — those are marked project-unique rather than dropped, so the full capability surface of each renderer (especially ruster's CPU/SIMD/wgpu/CUDA/hybrid backends) stays visible in the aggregate stats.

project.description: Codebase this record came from, e.g. 'ruster', 'fractals-rs', 'fractalrenderercpp', 'cpp', 'zigger', 'nanobrot', 'fraqtive'.

impl.description: Unique identifier for the specific implementation variant within the project, e.g. 'ruster-cpu-rayon', 'ruster-simd-f32x8-ilp', 'ruster-wgpu', 'ruster-cuda', 'ruster-hybrid-cpu+wgpu', 'ruster-hybrid-cpu+cuda', 'ruster-hybrid-heterogeneous', 'ruster-perturbation-cpu'. This is the column/row key used for ruster's own multi-backend leaderboard.

run_id.description: Source run directory / batch identifier, e.g. 'criterion_20260622_200733_1e927cb'.

path.description: Path to the native result file(s) this record was derived from, for traceability back to raw data.

detail.description: Free-text compute variant label straight from the native tool, e.g. 'rayon', 'f32x8_ilp', 'cuda', 'threads=8'.

device.description: Physical device this backend actually executed on. Load-bearing: until 2026-08-08 this machine had no NVIDIA Vulkan ICD, so gpu-wgpu ran on the integrated AMD Vega while gpu-cuda ran on the discrete RTX 3050 — the two were never the same GPU, and rows from those runs must not be compared.

param.description: Extra free-form axis that doesn't fit elsewhere, e.g. thread count for thread_scaling, zoom level for perturbation sweeps.

class.description: 'baseline-common': same fractal/resolution/max_iter/precision/naive-CPU-algorithm as at least one other project — goes in the fair cross-project table. 'project-unique': a real measurement but no other project has an equivalent (e.g. ruster's wgpu/CUDA/hybrid/perturbation backends) — still reported, just in the full-capability table instead. 'unclassified': the aggregator couldn't confidently classify this record (unrecognized naming convention) — still kept, flagged for manual review.

baseline_key.description: Grouping key for the fair-comparison table, e.g. 'mandelbrot@1920x1080@iter1000@f64@naive-cpu'. Null unless class == 'baseline-common'.

note.description: Why this is/isn't comparable — e.g. 'Google Benchmark repetitions give stddev but not a bootstrap CI, unlike Criterion'.

mean_ci_low_ms.description: Null if the native tool doesn't produce a bootstrap CI (e.g. plain Google Benchmark).

gflops_note.description: Why GFLOPs is null when it is — e.g. 'iteration count not exposed by this harness'.

status.description: 'no-data' marks a placeholder row for a project/impl that hasn't been instrumented yet (e.g. nanobrot, fraqtive) so it still appears in the leaderboard instead of silently vanishing.
